newsitem.title: USA: MaxServ calls Sears' $7 per share offer inadequate.
newsitem.headline: MaxServ calls Sears' $7 per share offer inadequate.

text.p: MaxServ Inc., a consumer appliance service provider, said Tuesday that Sears, Roebuck and Co.'s $7-a-share takeover offer was inadequate and urged shareholders to reject the hostile bid.
Sears on Feb. 4 said it launched its first hostile takeover bid to buy 35.6 percent of MaxServ stock that it does not already own for about $27 million, or $7 a share.
In a statement Tuesday, MaxServ said, "Proposed consideration of $7.00 in cash is inadequate to the MaxServ shareholders other than Sears."

Austin, Texas-based MaxServ said a special committee of the company's board of directors reviewed the deal and received a written opinion from its financial adviser, Broadview Associates LLC, that led it to reject the offer from Sears.
MaxServ said the special committee will continue to negotiate with Sears to attempt to get a better offer for the company's shares.
MaxServ provides information services and diagnostic assistance for consumer appliances.
On Monday, MaxServ said it planned to build a new headquarters and operations centre in Round Rock, Texas, northeast of Austin. The company plans to move into its new headquarters in mid-1998.
MaxServ stock rose 18.75 cents to $7.625 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq. Sears stock was down 12.5 cents at $54.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
